author: Hans O
title: multiprocessing while streaming
text:

I am developing a project using Python 3 and the tweepy API to get stock ticker info at certain times triggered by a tweet. I'm trying to get the ticker info at the time of a tweet as well as a certain period of time afterwards while still being able to stream at the same time. Here is the relevant code. def search_tweet(json_data): ticker = "" ... # searching criteria p = Process(target=get_time_info, args = (20,ticker)) p.start() p.join() def get_time_info(period,ticker): get_stock_info(ticker) #gets desired information about the ticker time.sleep(period) . #waits 20 seconds print(ticker + ": " + str(period) + " seconds later") get_stock_info(ticker) class TwitterStreamer(): def stream_tweets(self,tweetsFile, keywords,users): listener = TwitterListener(tweetsFile) auth = OAuthHandler(access_second.consumer_key, access_second.consumer_secret) auth.set_access_token(access_second.access_token, access_second.access_token_secret) stream = Stream(auth, listener) stream.filter(track=keywords) class TwitterListener(StreamListener): def __init__(self,tweetsFile): self.tweetsFile = tweetsFile def on_data(self, data): try: with open(self.tweetsFile, 'a') as tf: search_tweet(json.loads(data)) return(True) except BaseException as e: print("Error on data: " + str(e)) return(True) if __name__ == '__main__': keywords = ['AAPL'] file = "tweetsFile.json" users = [] twitterStreamer = TwitterStreamer() twitterStreamer.stream_tweets(file,keywords,users)
My issue right now is I know I'm using multiprocessing incorrectly as when the join method is called in search_tweet the program still waits for it to terminate, effectively making it the same as if I just called the method without creating a new process. This method does work somewhat if I get rid of join() but this is plain bad practices and results in zombie programs and eventually starts giving odd errors after some time.
Is it possible to call the join method at a different point when get_time_info has already finished and the entire program doesn't wait for it to terminate? Or do I simply need to re-imagine my solution to the problem?
